title: The pawn fork

card.idea: A pawn attacks the two squares diagonally in front of it. Push it so that both of those squares hold something, and one of them is lost. Nobody wants to take a pawn back with a knight, so the cheapest piece on the board is the rudest forker.
card.habit: Level two begins here — basic tactics are now allowed.

explain.text: The pawn on c4 attacks b5 and d5 now. Push it one square and it attacks b6 and d6 instead — and a knight is standing on each. Black moves one knight and White takes the other.
A pawn fork only works if the pawn survives. Here e5-e6 is check and hits the rook on d7, and the king cannot take, because the pawn on d5 is defending e6. Push a defended pawn.

challenges.prompt: Tap the square the c-pawn goes to so that it attacks both black knights.

hints.text: A pawn attacks the two squares diagonally ahead of it, never the one straight in front.

challenges.reason: From c5 the pawn attacks b6 and d6, and a knight is on each.

wrong.Ra6: The rook attacks one knight. Black defends it or moves it, and you have won nothing.

challenges.reason: c5 hits b6 and d6 at once. Black can only save one knight.

challenges.prompt: Tap every black piece the e-pawn would attack from e6.

hints.text: Two squares only: the ones diagonally in front of e6.

challenges.reason: From e6 the pawn attacks d7 and f7 — the rook and the king.

wrong.d6: The wrong pawn. From d6 it attacks c7 and e7, and nothing is on either.

challenges.reason: e6 is check and attacks the rook. The king must move, and the pawn takes on d7.

challenges.prompt: White pushes the pawn to e6, check. Is the pawn safe on e6?
reasons: No. Nothing defends e6, so the king just takes the pawn.
Yes. The pawn on d5 defends e6, so the king cannot take and has to step away.
No. The rook on d7 takes the pawn.

hints.text: Ask what is defending e6 before you push. One white pawn already is.

challenges.reason: A king may never move onto a defended square, so Kxe6 is not a legal move here.

challenges.prompt: One push wins a piece. Find it.

wrong.Rd1: Rd1 hangs the rook with check — Rxd1 is checkmate on the back rank. Look for a move that attacks two pieces at once.

challenges.reason: c5 attacks the knight on b6 and the rook on d6. Black saves the rook, White takes the knight.

challenges.prompt: White plays f5-f6. What has the pawn done?
options: Check to the king on g7, and it attacks the queen on e7 as well.
Check to the king on g7, and nothing else.
Nothing at all. The king takes the pawn on f6.

hints.text: From f6 a white pawn attacks e7 and g7. Look at what stands on both.

challenges.reason: The pawn on e5 defends f6, so the king cannot take, and taking with the queen loses her to exf6.

takeaway: Push the pawn where both of its two squares are worth something — and make sure something defends it first.
